text:
incident-bot: Paging @leo (oncall) — elevated 5xx rate observed on streaming-gateway (streaming API) starting ~2475001050. Metric: streaming_5xx_rate spike to 7.8% (baseline ~0.3%). Multiple customers reporting streaming disconnects and truncated responses. Severity: S2.

leo: Got it, on it. Can someone grab the gateway and upstream logs? I’ll start a triage.

aisha: Looking now — prelim logs show a cluster of `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `client closed connection` around the same window. Example log snippet from gateway-proxy-3: 
```
2026-03-15T01:04:12Z gateway-proxy-3 ERROR upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.12.5.23, server: stream-api
2026-03-15T01:04:12Z gateway-proxy-3 WARN client closed connection: 10.12.5.23: canceled by client, request id=abc123
```
Seems like chunked transfer frames were cut off.

tom: Also seeing increased 502/504 from the gateway LB to runtime pool. Rolling count of 502s matches the streaming spike.

leo: Any recent deploys/config changes around 00:55? ops-bot, any deploy activity?

ops-bot: Deploy notice: deploy/gateway-proxy v2.8.1 rolled at 2475000900 by rafael (config tweak: proxy_buffering toggle).

rafael: That was me — small change: disabled proxy_buffering for streaming endpoints to avoid buffer-induced latency (nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;`). Rolled to 4 pods. No errors observed in canary but might be correlated.

emma: If proxy_buffering off was applied cluster-wide it could increase upstream connection churn because we forward chunks immediately. We also adjusted keepalive settings in the same patch. I’ll check the diff.

aisha: Dumping a few gateway-backend tcp resets from kernel logs: `RST, ACK` from upstream IPs at the same time windows. Upstream runtime shows logged `connection reset by peer` and some OOM-kill events on a subset of model-worker pods — seems like memory pressure coincident with the change.

tom: So hypothesis: disabling buffering increased memory/traffic patterns on workers -> upstreams reset -> gateway sees truncated chunked streams -> clients get disconnects/5xx. That would explain client cancellations.

leo: Immediate mitigation options? We need to reduce customer impact while we investigate.

emma: We can do a quick live mitigation: 1) route streaming traffic to fallback paged endpoint (non-streaming) for affected tenants so they get full responses albeit higher latency — this prevents partial stream disconnects. 2) roll back the proxy_buffering change to restore previous behavior. 3) scale up runtime worker autoscaler pool to absorb spike. I can execute 1 and 3 now.

leo: Do 1) and 3). Rafael, revert the config to previous if you can do it fast; otherwise we rollback gateway-proxy. I’ll page platform oncall to help with scaling.

rafael: Rolling back to proxy_buffering:on on streaming route now. Command: 
```bash
kubectl -n gateway set env deploy/gateway-proxy PROXY_BUFFERING=on --record
kubectl -n gateway rollout restart deploy/gateway-proxy
```
Rollout started.

emma: Routing change: creating temporary route rule for high-risk tenants to use /v1/paged-generate. Patch applied via edge-router: `route: tenant in (acct-*) -> upstream: paged-service`. Pushed at 2475001205.

ops-bot: Autoscaler: increasing runtime-workers minReplicas from 6 -> 12 for pool=streaming-workload. Scaling started at 2475001210.

aisha: After rollback and routing change I see 5xx rate dropping — currently down to 1.2% and trending down. Streaming disconnect reports from customers also decreasing.

tom: Confirmed: gateway 502s reduced and runtime OOM events stopped after scaling. Looks like a combination of pressure + buffering change.

leo: Good. Assigning incident commander: @emma. Emma, take lead for remaining mitigation and timeline to restore streaming with buffering off if possible.

emma: Taking this. Next steps: 1) run a controlled canary of the buffering-off config only for low-risk tenants with scaled worker pool and memory limits tightened; 2) add stricter circuit-breaker for chunked upstream resets to fallback to paged response automatically; 3) postmortem.

rafael: I’ll prepare a canary patch that toggles proxy_buffering off only for `canary-tenant` and sets `keepalive_timeout 75s` and `proxy_connect_timeout` slightly higher. Will also add resource limits on runtime worker containers.

leo: Good. Customer comms — any impacted customers known? Aisha, can you surface top 5 tenants affected?

aisha: Top impacted: acct-tex (heavy streaming tests), acct-zen, acct-halo. I've opened support tickets and flagged on status.redwood.ai. Noted: no data leakage, only service degradation.

ops-bot: Incident tracker created: INC-2475, severity: S2, started: 2475001050, commander: emma.

emma: Putting short-term mitigation tasks: 
- keep routing to paged for heavy tenants until canary completes
- confirm rollback fully rolled out (waiting for all gateway pods ready)
- schedule follow-up for canary in 30m

leo: Handing on-call to @emma — I have a meeting. Leave escalation to me if anything spikes >10% 5xx or full region failure.

emma: I’m taking oncall. Will monitor dashboards and update every 10m.

rafael: Canary patch ready, will deploy to 1 pod group after 5m steady metrics.

aisha: Current metrics at 2475001320: streaming_5xx_rate 0.8%, runtime_oom_count 0, gateway_502_count reduced by 85% vs peak. Customer tickets still trickling but reduced.

emma: Status update: mitigation in place, customer impact mitigated via routing fallback and scaling, rollback completed. Next actions: run canary for buffered-off config with tight resource limits, add circuit breaker to fallback on first chunked reset, and root cause analysis on why worker memory spiked under buffering-off.

leo: Thanks team. I’ll join if needed. Emma, own the postmortem and include timeline and recommendations (canary policies, resource thresholds, automated fallback).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2475 updated: severity S2 -> mitigation in place. Postmortem squad assigned to emma, rafael, aisha, tom.

emma: Taking notes and will send a summary in #postmortems in ~2 hours with a preliminary RCA.

-- end of thread --
